title: From Europe to Paraguay and Matto-Grosso
short_title: From Europe to Paraguay and Matto-Grosso

p0026a.what: printed page 16, a blank leaf in the Cornell copy

summary: Marion Mulhall (about 1844–1922), an Irishwoman living in Buenos Aires, describes a journey made about 1876 from Lisbon to Brazil and the River Plate, and then some two thousand miles up the Paraná and Paraguay rivers to Asunción, Corumbá, and Cuiabá, in the Brazilian province of Mato Grosso, where, by her account, no Englishwoman had been before. On the way she visits Sintra, Rio de Janeiro, Montevideo, an estancia in Uruguay, General Urquiza on the river Uruguay, Buenos Aires, and Córdoba. She writes about the towns, the river steamers, Paraguay after its war, the Guaycurú, Payaguá, Guató, and other Indian peoples, and the ruins of the Jesuit missions. Her husband gave her his notes to compare with hers. The book has ten engravings, a map, and a table of distances.
